overall: The AG found neither the Board of Selectmen nor the Capital Improvement Planning Committee violated the Open Meeting Law on any of the four allegations; no remedial action was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board cancelled, without discussion, a listed agenda item on March 29, 2011, and did not let him speak as scheduled.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Board was not required to discuss the items listed on the March 29, 2011 agenda or to reschedule the complainant's appointment to speak.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated the law by dropping the 'Citizen's Input' agenda item on April 12, 2011 and not taking public comment at the opening.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee violated the law by denying his request for more speaking time at its April 26, 2011 meeting and lacking a citizen input item.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law permits the chair of the Committee to decide who can speak at a meeting and for how long.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee's April 26, 2011 meeting notice was defective because it listed no adjournment time.
allegations.key_passage: The law does not require a public body to list an adjournment time on a meeting notice.
